What checking costs

Checking is free: ESPN's schedules, and The Odds API's own league and game lists once your Worker passes them through. Load odds uses The Odds API credits (about 1 per bet type, only when the league has games). BettingPros board uses your BettingPros calls. A league with no free schedule is listed as not checked: it may still have games, so Load odds finds out.

Parlays pick'em apps (PrizePicks, Pick6, Underdog, Sleeper) pay a fixed multiple; combo apps (Kalshi, Novig, Polymarket, DK and FD Predictions, Fliff, Bovada) pay the legs' odds multiplied

How it is figured

How it's figured: each pick's chance is the board's own estimate (the market price, pulled toward BettingPros' model by your model weight in Settings). An entry adds up every way it can finish, all hit, and for Flex one or two misses, each with its exact chance. Break-even is the chance every pick would need for the entry to pay back what it costs. Suggested stakes use your Kelly fraction and edge haircut, kept between your smallest and largest bet. Picks are treated as independent, so keep one pick per game.

🔓 Parole 🎣 fishing: you're the Maker — post La Contadora's bait price on Novig and see who bites. Only a bet once someone takes it.

Who gets parole

Only Jail reasons a price can fix get parole: below your floor or minimum, odds range, and outliers / risk-bet limit (the bait must then beat the market, at your minimum stake). One-per-player, game caps, the daily max, the outlier limit and started games stay in Jail. The screener never places anything.

How Live edges works

The board's model is pre-game, so once a game starts it is stale; here the fair price is ESPN's live win chance (moneylines only). A price is marked ✓ edge only with at least 3% edge after the fee, a chance between 8% and 92% (near the end one play decides it) and a price within 10 points of ESPN's (further off is a different or stale market). Each game shows when ESPN's number last changed; if it has not changed for 2 minutes while the game kept going, its edges are hidden (halftime and timeouts do not count). The stale check needs about 2 minutes of watching a game before it works: in the first 2 minutes after you open the app, a stale ESPN number can look fresh. In soccer, a quiet stretch with no goal can also show stale; that is on purpose, to be safe. Leagues: every football, basketball, hockey, baseball and soccer league ESPN covers, worldwide; one with nothing live is skipped for 10 minutes. Where ESPN has no live win chance (often soccer), Pinnacle alone is the fair price. Pinnacle is asked only when you press Scan, at most 40 times a day on this device (your pinnapi plan has a daily limit); Auto-refresh uses ESPN, which is free. Pinnacle live: once your Worker has it, Pinnacle's live price (vig removed) becomes the fair price and ESPN must agree; until then it is ESPN alone. Prices move in seconds: before you bet, check the app still sells it at or under pay at most. ESPN's number is a model too and cannot see injuries or who is on the field, so bet smaller than usual (half your normal stake is a fair start). With Auto-refresh on, the scan repeats every 30 seconds at most while this tab is open.

Live your open bets, with ESPN's live scores and stats — uses no BettingPros API calls

How to read the bars

On each bar, green is where the stat needs to finish and red is where the bet loses. The white bar is where it is now; ▲ is the projection (stat so far + the line × the part of the game left — rough: it can't see injuries, blowouts or overtime). Win %, cover % and over % are ESPN's live numbers, for ESPN's line. A cash-out offer shows its break-even %: keep the bet only if you think it wins more often than that.

How sync works

One copy of your bet log lives in your Cloudflare store. Any device with the screener passphrase and this password sees the same bets, baits and settings. Changes upload a few seconds after you make them; other devices pick them up when they open or come back to the page, and once a minute while it's open — Wi-Fi or cellular.

Synced: bet log, removed bets, parlay marks, Parole baits, which book fills are matched, your settings (bankroll, La Contadora's rules, fees) and the last board you loaded with its grading history. Stays on each device: the screener passphrase, this password, theme, team logos.

First time: on the Mac run cd ~/prop-bet-api, then npx wrangler secret put SYNC_KEY (type the password you picked — it never goes in chat or code), then npx wrangler deploy. Turn it on here on the PC first (its log becomes the cloud copy), then on the phone. Lost a device? Run the secret command again with a new password.

Screens odds range, EV floor, books, fees

  
A bet has to clear all of these. Widening them until something appears is how you end up on the rows that only look good.

  

    

    

    

    

    

  

  

    
    

    
    
  

  

    
    
    
    
    
        
  

  

    Platform fees — verify these on each site before trusting a net number
    

      

      

      

      

      

      

      

    

    
Kalshi runs on a curve rather than a flat rate: 7% × price × (1 − price) per contract, which is 7% × (1 − price) of what you put up. A short favorite costs about 2.3%, an even-money bet 3.5%, a +400 longshot 5.6%. The fee is charged on top of the contract cost, so net EV is (gross − fee) ÷ (1 + fee). Kalshi also rounds each order's fee up to the next cent; the board includes that when it counts whole contracts.
Polymarket US uses the same curve at 6.95% (since Sep 17, 2026 — your Oct 25 Kenneth Walker fill paid $0.16 on 9.28 shares at 49¢, which is 6.95%). Novig is free before the game; once it's live, takers pay 6% × price × (1 − price) (from Novig's own market data) — added automatically for live bets in + Add a bet and the bet editor.

  






  
Stake sizing bankroll and Kelly

  
Kelly scales a bet to its edge. The haircut shrinks that edge first, because the fair values behind it move and the biggest ones move most. What survives gets clamped to the range you actually bet in.

  

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

    

  

  
How stakes are sized
One daily max for everything (v3.11): the API board, the pasted Market EV page and exchange fills all count against the same %, so a big paste can't stack on top of the board. Stakes size off a blend: the market's no-vig price pulled toward BettingPros' number by the model weight (0.35 = mostly market). If there's no market price for a bet, the model number is used with the haircut. Bets on a game you already have money on are trimmed so the game stays under the per-game max.

How the list is sorted, and soccer grading
The sport list is sorted by the next game (ESPN, free): sports playing soonest on top, off-season ones at the bottom marked no games. A load for a sport with no game in the next 24 hours is skipped so it doesn't spend calls (you can still load it anyway). Soccer is graded on regular time (90' + stoppage): extra time and penalties don't count, a draw loses a team's moneyline, and quarter-goal handicaps (±0.25 / ±0.75) are left for you to grade.

Lines

  
How edge is figured
"Edge" is the real answer to "is this good value": a fair win probability with the vig stripped out, compared against what this specific book is offering. Pinnacle is the sharp reference (its line devigged, pulled via pinnapi.com); Consensus is the devigged average of every book we pull, and is the fallback when Pinnacle data isn't available. BettingPros' own EV/Cover % (its model's opinion) are shown for reference only.

Edges are net of fees, using the same fee inputs as the Board tab (Kalshi's price-based curve, the rest as you've set them) — hover an edge to see its gross and fee. Only games that haven't kicked off are shown. Pinnacle's line is a pre-game line, and comparing it against live in-play prices produces fake edges (a game 80 minutes in once showed a 168% "edge"). Stale quotes are dropped automatically, and any edge over 10% is flagged with ⚠ — on a moneyline that's almost always a bad quote, so confirm the price on the book before betting.

What counts here
Every single of that game day, plus each leg of a parlay built on the Parlays tab (they keep their chance). The band is our fair chance when you logged it (Augi's 5-point bands). Bets typed in with no cover, and parlays typed in by hand, are Unknown. A band is a label, not a rule: the bet was already OK by La Contadora, or your own call.

Game daysBetsPendingW–L–PStakedProfitROI

  
How these are counted
By the day the game is played (Central time), weeks from Monday. Profit and ROI count settled bets only (wins with fees, losses, pushes, sales, money lost cancelling); bets still to play or in play are Pending, not lost. Free bets are not money staked and count their winnings only.

  
Import bets from a file
    
An Odds Board bet-import file (JSON, the kind Augi's assistant makes from screenshots of your slips). Check each ticket's game day, book, cost and total return before saving. A ticket already in your log is left unticked. New ones start with no result and are graded like any bet you type in (ESPN, or Look out). A version 2 file can also hold moneylines, spreads and totals, tickets already settled (result and profit as the book shows them), free and bonus bets, and fixes to bets already in your log (each fix lists what it changes, and the bet keeps the old values in its edit history).

What counts here

Is the model honest?

  
How this is measured
What BettingPros' Cover % promised vs. how often those picks actually won — on recommended bets only, so it tests the screener's selection, not the model across every prop. Uses every pick on your boards that got graded when its game went final, plus your own graded bets (sold bets excluded). Rows under 100 picks are a first look, not a verdict.

Bet result study 5-point cover bands · did each band win as often as it said?

  

  

    
Projected coverLoggedPendingW–L–PAvg predictionHit rateDifferenceProfit

    
  

  
How this is figured
Singles only. Average prediction, hit rate and difference use graded wins and losses; pushes, sold and pending bets are left out. Difference is the hit rate minus the average prediction, in points. Profit is the settled money (betProfit: fees, boosts and free bets counted as in the Bet log). Game days, not the day the bet was placed. Small groups swing hard: read it after hundreds of bets, like the Scorecard.




   
  
Entry-price bands book fills that matched no board card · price benchmark, not forecast calibration

  

    
Entry priceTicketsPendingW–L–PAvg break-evenHit rateStakeProfitROI

    
  

  
Each fill’s band is the win rate its price needed to break even, fee included. Hit rate above the average break-even means these won more than their prices needed; it does not say they had an edge when taken. Each ticket counts (two tickets on one bet count twice). Sold bets count in tickets and money only. The entry price is not used in the cover bands, the calibration, EV or the Scorecard: these bets still sit in the study’s “no cover saved” row and in the Scorecard’s “Own / unverified” line. Same game days as the study above.




   
  
◎ Rings and extras Perfectas against the other best bets · Just missed and Hail Marys, each on its own record

  

  
How this is figured
Singles only, since v4.50. A best bet logged from the board keeps its ◎ checks from that moment (6 of 6 is a Perfecta). 🍀 Just missed and 🔮 Hail Marys are the extras a mode offers: real bets, in your money, the calendar and the Today card like any other, but kept out of the Scorecard above, so its 1,000-bet test only judges La Contadora's best bets. Their lines here are only the ones you chose to place (a user-selected subset: the result may reflect your selection, not the mode); every Watch bet, chosen or not, is in the Watch bets panel below as a $1 shadow record. Profit and ROI count settled bets only (free bets count their winnings). Bets from your books, typed in, or older than v4.50 have no ring recorded and are not listed here. Small groups swing hard: the ring means something only if it keeps beating the rest over hundreds of bets.




   
  
👀 Watch bets: model vs market bets the model liked but the market-adjusted edge did not · saved once, graded, never bet

  

  
How this is figured
Each Watch bet is saved once, the first time it shows (one per player or team, stat, side, exact line and game), with the price you were shown and the model, market and blend chances. That first snapshot is never changed. Later looks only note when the price or a forecast moved. After the game it is graded like your bets. It is never a bet: not in the Bet log, profit, ROI, the calendar or the daily max.
The Brier score is the squared miss of a forecast (0 is perfect); lower wins. The headline averages market − model inside each game, then across games, so a game with many props counts once; its 95% range comes from 5,000 resamples of games. Above zero means the model forecast these better. Stages need both counts: Directional at 100 bets in 50 games; Useful at 300 in 150 with the range clear of zero; Credible at 1,000 in 500, the range clear of zero and within ±0.005, and the closing line and ROI pointing the same way. "Materially" means the range starts beyond 0.001. These rules were set before any results.
One pick per game: 5 minutes before kickoff, the Watch bet with the highest conservative EV, at the price last seen. Seen within 30 minutes of kickoff it is a primary pick; 31 to 120 minutes, a stale fallback, kept apart; older or never, no pick. The app has to be open near kickoff (or have seen the price earlier), so this covers the games you looked at. Closing prices come free from Kalshi, Polymarket US and Novig in the last 10 minutes; sportsbook closes would cost credits, so they are not taken for Watch bets.

About CLV and variance   
  
CLV here compares your price to the closing price on the same side, in implied-probability terms. It is not devigged, so a positive number is evidence rather than proof — but a screen that consistently beats the close is finding real prices, and one that does not is finding noise no matter what the EV column said.

  
Expect a few hundred bets before any of this separates from variance.
